reasons: A and B are nearly word-for-word the same. Both open by catching the trap: 6 points at most (Order 163, Article 25), so 10 points only come down to 4. Both say the extra margin rises from 2 to 8 points, explain clearing day, compute 3 hours of study plus exams, and give correct 12123 steps. They share the same gaps: no mention of on-site study (2 points) or public-service activities, nothing on the service being free, and the application conditions leave out the three-cycle bar for drunk driving, hit-and-run and point buying. They also add the same Beijing- and Shenzhen-specific details (24-hour resit window, 5-minute minimum session, 7-working-day exam deadline). The only difference is the table's total row: A writes 222–330 minutes as exact figures and B rounds to 3.7–5.5 hours, and both are arithmetically correct. That leaves a tie.
